natsuki.title: Scars and Bets
natsuki.text:
Natsuki takes you up onto the old ramparts at sunset, where the stone is still warm from the afternoon. She sits down on the edge with her legs over the drop, as she used to sit on the wall behind the school.

She pulls up the hem of her shirt to show you a scar below her ribs. It's pale and ragged. She got it in her first week here, from something with too many teeth, before she had learned how to hold a sword.

"Nobody stitched it. I didn't know who to ask." She lets the shirt fall. "Three years, Sam. Cold hostels. Contracts I couldn't read. I got good because the alternative was dying."

You remember the two of you on the curb outside the corner shop, with ice pops melting down your wrists.

"I kept thinking, if Sam walked up right now, he'd do something stupid and we'd somehow both come out breathing." She laughs, roughly, and leans into your shoulder. "Then you finally turn up, and you've inherited a brothel."
ngpp: She's laughing about the ice pops when she stops mid-sentence. She looks at the stone under her, then at the lantern on the wall, and frowns. "Weird," she says. "Felt like I'd sat here before. Like someone tugged my sleeve." Then she shrugs it off and steals a look at you.

"I remember every stupid bike race back home," she says slowly. "Every one. But this wall, this bench, you next to me, that feels remembered too, and it shouldn't." She twists the hem of her shirt in her fist. "Sam, have we done this already?"

"Three years alone didn't shake me loose," Natsuki says, leaning on your arm. "Whatever happened before this didn't either. I remember Earth. I remember this wall, too, and you sitting right here. Don't look at me like that, idiot. I know what I know."

choices.label: Trace the scar gently with your eyes only
choices.res: You don't touch it. You look, and you let her see you looking. She goes quiet in a way she never was on the old street. She keeps her shirt hem in her fist a moment longer than she needs to. Then she nudges the plaster on her cheek back into place and says, "Okay. That's enough of that," and she doesn't sound annoyed at all.

choices.label: Admit the dumb thing was on purpose
choices.res: "Totally on purpose," you say. "I planned the whole thing. Other world, brothel, everything." {N} stares at you for a second. Then she grins, rubs the plaster on her cheek and punches your shoulder, softer than she'd like to admit. "Idiot. You couldn't plan a sandwich." She leaves her shoulder against yours afterward, and neither of you mentions it.

image.comp: showing him a scar on her arm, sitting on a fence, half-smiling

natsuki.title: Incoming
natsuki.text:
You walk into the washroom without knocking. You've been walking into rooms that Natsuki is in since you were six.

She's in the bath. Steam is rising, her chestnut hair is plastered to her forehead, and she's humming something from a cartoon you both watched.

The soap is already in the air.

She doesn't mean anything by it. It's fifteen years of reflex. When you were nine it was a pillow, and when you were twelve it was a shoe. The difference is that she now throws at adventurer speed, and that she is not nine.

Behind the soap, coming toward your face, you can see hers. It's very small and very red. Her other arm has gone across her chest. Her mouth is open, and she's about to call you something she hasn't called you since middle school.

1.title: Soap & Pride
1.text:
You open the washroom door. Natsuki is in the bath with her hair pinned up and her towel thrown over the bench, out of reach.

She goes for the soap out of pure reflex. Her arm comes back. Then she stops, with her cheeks burning, and drops her hand into the water with a huff.

"Quit grinning like that, idiot." She sinks down until the water's at her chin and glares at you over it. "Fine. If you're coming in, make yourself useful. There's a spot between my shoulder blades I haven't been able to reach in three years." She turns her bare back to you, and her ears are scarlet.

choices.label: Kneel beside the tub and scrub her scarred back gently
choices.res: You open the door wider and kneel beside the tub with the brush. Natsuki stiffens for two stubborn seconds as the lather goes over her back, over the sword calluses and the pale scars. Then her shoulders drop. She tips her head back against your arm with a sharp breath, her wet hair on your sleeve, and turns her face up toward yours.
choices.fallbackRes: She grumbles the whole time about your terrible technique. Press harder, then lighter, then harder again. She leans back against your knuckles all the same, and by the end her ears are pink and she's stopped complaining. "Okay," she says. "That was fine. Don't tell anyone I said that."

choices.label: Toss her the bath brush and close the door cleanly
choices.res: You toss the brush into the tub. It lands with a splash near her knee, and you step back and pull the door shut. "Chicken!" she yells through the wood. She's laughing, and you hear her kicking water. A second later, quieter: "Thanks. For not making it weird." You're not sure she meant you to hear that.

3.title: No More Clothes Between Us
3.text:
Steam rolls out when you open the washroom door.

Natsuki is sitting in the deep wooden tub with one scarred leg hooked over the rim. She's naked and she isn't covering anything. Water is running down her tits and over the hard muscle of her stomach. She looks up at you through her wet fringe with the grin she used to get before a race.

"Took you long enough, Sam." She flicks water at you. "I waited three years in this city. I'm not waiting for you to fold your clothes. Strip off and get in here before it goes cold. I've got plans for you, and they're not gentle."

choices.label: Strip down and climb straight into the tub with her
choices.res: You strip fast, and she watches every piece of clothing hit the floor. The water is almost too hot when you climb in. Natsuki doesn't wait for you to settle. She grabs your shoulders and pushes you back against the wooden wall, her wet tits against your chest and her mouth at your ear. "Told you," she says. "Not gentle."

choices.label: Pin her lightly against the rim and take your time
choices.res: You press her back against the rim of the tub, slowly, one hand on the wood beside her head. The other slides down her wet stomach, and she hisses and grips the back of your neck hard. The steam hides nothing. "Take your time," she says. "I'll hate it. I'll hate it more if you stop." Her heels slip on the tub floor.

choices.label: Duck
choices.res: You duck, but not fast enough. The soap clips your ear and skitters across the tiles. {N} makes a noise that's half apology and half laugh, and she presses the heel of her hand to her mouth. "Sorry! Reflex!" Her face is still red, and she's already sliding lower in the water. "Next time, knock. I mean it this time."

choices.label: Take it like a man
choices.res: You stand there and let it come. The soap hits you right between the eyes with a smack you can hear in the hall. "Nice reflexes, hero," she says, sinking up to her nose in the water. Her amber eyes are bright, and she's shaking with laughter. When you wipe your face she's still looking, and she doesn't look away first.

choices.label: Apologize through the door
choices.res: You back out, shut the door, and say sorry to the wood. For a moment there's only dripping. "Knock next time, idiot!" She sounds like she's grinning. You hear the soap plop into the tub, and then her voice again, lower. "You're forgiven. Go away. Not far away, though."

image.comp: throwing a bar of soap at adventurer speed from a bath, furious and blushing

natsuki.title: Almost Taiyaki
natsuki.text:
In the evening market the two of you find a stall selling something that is almost taiyaki. The shape is wrong, and it's more a frog than a fish. But the batter is right, and the smell stops you both in the middle of the street.

Natsuki buys ten.

She eats four of them standing up, without saying a word, and she looks happier than you've seen her since she arrived.

Halfway through the fifth she goes quiet. The paper bag crumples slowly in her fist.

"This is going to sound dumb." She isn't looking at you. She's watching a lantern bob away down the street. "Back in high school I just assumed how it would go. I'd end up nagging you over dinner every night. About vegetables, and your posture. I never decided it. I thought it was obvious." She swallows. "Then I walked down one alley, and I spent three years thinking I'd thrown it away. Dumb, right?"

choices.label: Pull her into the empty alley behind the stall and prove she was right
choices.res: You catch her wrist before she can turn away and draw her behind the stall, into the alley where the lantern light gives out. She lets you. You put her back against the brick and kiss her until the paper bag drops and the last taiyaki rolls into the gutter. "Not dumb," you say against her mouth. "Say it again," she says, and pulls you in by the hoodie.

choices.label: Tell her it isn't dumb
choices.res: "It isn't dumb." Your voice cracks on the second word. Natsuki crushes the paper bag into a ball and says nothing. She stares at the lantern until it's gone around the corner. But when you take her hand she doesn't pull away, and after a minute her thumb starts moving over your knuckles, the way it did when you were kids.

choices.label: Steal the last taiyaki to break the tension
choices.res: You reach into the bag, take the last one and bite its head off before she can stop you. {N} yells. She chases you three stalls down the street, past a woman selling cabbages, who yells too. When she catches you she's laughing so hard she can't hit you. Her ears are red. "That was supposed to be mine," she says, and takes the tail.

image.comp: eating fish-shaped pastries at a street stall with him, cheeks full, going quiet
image.setting: busy market street, food stalls, afternoon

natsuki.title: Solo Run
natsuki.text:
Natsuki took a dungeon contract without telling anyone. It was a solo run with a deep floor, and the bounty had sat on the guild board for a month because nobody else would touch it.

She's gone for three days. You find out where she went from the bartender.

She comes back through the front door on the third night with her arm in a sling made from her own cloak and a sack of gold over her shoulder. She's grinning through the grime. Her sword is chipped along one edge, and the plaster is gone from her cheek, along with some of the cheek.

"Basically nothing," she announces to the common room. "Two of them. Maybe five. Look at this haul!"

Then she sees your face.

The grin falters. She stands there with the sack still held up. She looks like a kid who has brought home a test with a hundred on it and found that nobody is pleased.
ngpp: When you pull the bandages out before she's finished talking, she blinks. She says nothing, but her eyes stay on your hands, as if she's watched them do this before. "Lucky guess," she mutters, and she doesn't sound like she believes it.

"You went to the bottom cupboard for the splint without looking," she says through gritted teeth. "We never kept it there. Did we?" She tries to grin, and it doesn't hold. "Sam, I feel like I've sat in this chair with this exact arm. It's creeping me out."

She drops into the chair before you say a word and holds out her good arm. "Yeah, yeah. I knew you'd look at me like that, idiot." Her voice is rough. "Don't ask how. I've done this before, I'm sure of it. So patch me up first. Then you can yell."

choices.label: Yell at her
choices.res: "You don't get to disappear on me twice!" It comes out wrong, too loud and too raw, and the whole common room goes quiet. {N} lowers the sack. She opens her mouth to shout back, and doesn't. She sets the gold on a table and walks upstairs with her good arm held stiff. You don't talk for the rest of the night.

choices.label: Patch her up, quietly
choices.res: You don't say anything. You take her to the kitchen, cut the cloak off her arm, clean the gash and bind it, and she lets you without a single joke. Her hand shakes once, and you hold it still. When you're done she leans her forehead against yours and breathes out, long and slow. The sack of gold sits forgotten on the floor.

choices.label: Make her promise
choices.res: "Next time, you come with me," she says, trying to laugh, and holds out her good hand. "Deal?" It isn't what you meant. But she looks at you like it's the only thing she has to offer. You say deal. She spits in her palm and you shake on it, and neither of you mentions how bad the sling looks.

image.comp: limping in with a broken arm in a sling and a sack of gold, defiant grin

natsuki.title: Fireworks
natsuki.text:
Natsuki has been up to something with the guild alchemist all week. It has cost her half her savings. Tonight she takes you up onto the east parapet with a sack of salty fried things and makes you sit down and wait.

"August," she says. "The river festival. We went every year. You always got the goldfish game wrong."

Down in the yard, the alchemist lights a fuse and runs.

The first shell splutters up green and lopsided and goes out with a cough. Natsuki swears at it.

The second one climbs. It keeps climbing, well past the rooftops. Then it opens into a wide pink chrysanthemum that lights every slate in Hollowmere and hangs there.

Shutters are opening all over town. Somebody cheers.

She doesn't say anything. Her boots are swinging over the drop, and her shoulder is against yours. In the light of the third shell you can see that her eyes are wet, and that she's smiling.

2.text:
Natsuki has bribed the guild alchemist into firing off homemade shells, like the August festival back home. She sits down on the east parapet close enough that her bare thigh is pressed along yours before the first fuse is lit.

The big pink one goes up and opens over the rooftops. All of Hollowmere turns to look at it.

Natsuki doesn't. She has turned to look at you. The light is moving on her face, and her eyes are bright.

"I planned this for a week," she says. "And now I don't care about the fireworks." Her hand closes in the front of your hoodie. "There's an empty watch-alcove about ten feet behind us. I checked."

choices.label: Hold her hand
choices.res: You take her hand. Her scarred fingers shake for one second, and then they lace between yours and hold. The finale goes up in gold and white, and the light runs over her cheek. She doesn't pull back or make a joke. She watches the sky, squeezes once, and keeps her hand where it is until the smoke drifts over the roofs.

choices.label: Tell her you missed her, all three years
choices.res: "I missed you," you say. "All three years. I didn't know where you were, and I missed you anyway." She hits your shoulder hard enough to sting. Then her face crumples, and she cries into your hoodie with her fist knotted in the fabric. The last rockets go off and drown her out. When she laughs, it's wet and angry and relieved all at once.

choices.label: Pull her down into the empty watch-alcove once the smoke clears
choices.res: The last pink ember is still sinking over the watchtower when Natsuki catches both sides of your collar. She doesn't say anything this time. She pulls you into the alcove, where the lantern light is a thin gold strip on the stone and the air smells of old rope and smoke. She gets her back against the wall and drags you in, her breath hot on your mouth.

image.comp: watching fireworks from the town wall with him, faces lit up
image.setting: town wall at night, colorful fireworks over rooftops

natsuki.title: Door Kicked In
natsuki.text:
Natsuki kicks your door open at dawn.

She has never been good at knocking, but this is new. The lock splinters under her boot. Cold light comes in behind her. She's red in the face, and her sword is still on her hip. She has plainly been up all night walking the walls and arguing with herself.

"I spent three years here thinking I'd never see you again." She's almost shouting. "And before that I spent a whole life back home pretending we were just kids from the same street. I knew, Sam. I knew when we were fifteen. I was too chicken to say it, so I said 'race you' for ten years."

She takes a breath that shakes.

"I'm not wasting another day. I love you, you idiot. I'm staying, and it's not for the free meals. It never was."

She kicks the door shut behind her. It doesn't latch any more, so she shoves the chair against it.
ngpp: The latch splinters, and she freezes with her boot still raised. Something about the sound is familiar. She shakes her head. "Huh," she says. "Weird. Feels like I've lost my temper at this exact dawn before." Then she goes on shouting at you.

"Don't ask why I feel like I've broken this door already," she growls. She's flushed to her collarbones, and she isn't looking at your face. "I know where the chair goes. I know you'll say nothing for ten seconds. I don't get how."

"I don't care how it works anymore," Natsuki says. She unbuckles her sword belt and lets it drop. "Earth, this town, whatever came before. I remember all of it, and I remember saying this to you. I'm saying it again, Sam. You're stuck with me."
natsuki.goLead: Natsuki drops her scabbard onto the chair and shoves you back onto the mattress. She climbs on top of you and straddles your waist, fierce and out of breath and laughing.

choices.label: Say yes
Not yet
choices.res: {N} scowls, then it drains out of her face. "I can wait," she says. "Don't make it long, idiot." She picks up her scabbard and looks at the wrecked latch. On the way out she tries to fix the door herself, badly, hammering it with her fist and muttering about patience.
